86.title: Being
86.text: Being, pure being — without any further determination. In its indeterminate immediacy it is equal only to itself, and also not unequal with respect to an other; it has no difference within it, nor again without it.

87.title: Nothing
87.text: Nothing, pure nothing: it is simply equality with itself, complete emptiness, absence of all determination and content — undifferentiatedness in itself.

88.title: Becoming
88.text: Pure Being and pure Nothing are, therefore, the same. What is the truth is neither Being nor Nothing, but that Being does not pass over, but has passed over, into Nothing; and Nothing does not pass over, but has passed over, into Being.

89.title: Determinate Being
89.text: In Becoming, Being and Nothing have each vanished into the other; their truth is this movement of immediate disappearance. The result of this movement is Determinate Being (Dasein) — Being in a form which is at rest, in which the two moments are held together in a single unity.

90.title: Reality and Negation
90.text: Determinate Being contains, as its two moments, Reality and Negation. Reality is the positive aspect — the being which something is; Negation is the negative aspect — the boundary which distinguishes it from an Other.

91.title: Something and Other
91.text: Determinate Being, taken as a whole, is Something; over against it stands an Other, which is itself also Something, and so on indefinitely. Something and its Other mutually determine one another.

92.title: Change
92.text: The relation of Something to its Other is neither fixed nor external: the Other is itself something else, and Change is precisely the passage from Something into an Other in which Something is at the same time preserved.

94.title: Infinity
94.text: The Infinite is not simply the absence of limitation, but the affirmative self-relation which contains the Finite within itself as a sublated moment. Bad infinity is the endless progression; true infinity is the circular self-return of the Concept.

95.title: Being-for-self
95.text: Being-for-self is the unity of Being and Determinate Being — a self-relatedness in which the negative moment has been taken back into the positive. Its simplest form is the One.

96.title: The One
96.text: The One is Being-for-self in its simplest form: the exclusion of all otherness, the sheer self-identity of the determinate being with itself.

97.title: Repulsion and Attraction
97.text: The One, in its relation to itself, repels itself from itself and posits a Many; but in repelling, it also attracts — the Many Ones are held together by the very act of repulsion.

98.title: Ideality
98.text: The Many Ones are not finally separate; their separation is sublated in the ideality of Being-for-self, which is the transition to Quantity.

99.title: Quantity
99.text: Quantity is Being in which the determinacy is no longer posited as one with Being itself, but as sublated — as indifferent to what the something is. Pure Quantity is the first form of this indifference: continuous magnitude.

107.title: Measure
107.text: Measure is the unity of Quality and Quantity — a Quantum to which a Quality is bound. In Measure, Quality and Quantity are no longer indifferent to one another; the specific quantum is what it is only because it has this determinate quality.

112.title: Essence as such
112.text: Essence is Being that has returned into itself — Being as sublated, as the self-identical ground of all determination. It is not immediate but reflective: what it is, it is only by negating the immediate and preserving it as its own moment.

115.title: Shine (Schein)
115.text: Shine (Schein) is Essence as it immediately appears — Being which is not positive but negative, not self-subsistent but a positedness. It is the reflection of Essence in itself, seen from the side of its immediacy.

119.title: Identity
119.text: Identity, as a determination of Essence, is not abstract equality but concrete self-identity — the sameness which contains difference within it as its own moment.

120.title: Difference
120.text: Difference is the negativity which Essence contains within itself. It appears first as Diversity (indifferent difference), then as Contrast (the difference of opposites), and finally as Contradiction.

122.title: Contradiction
122.text: Contradiction is the negative determination of Essence — the moment in which the positive and the negative are not merely opposed, but each is the other's own other, and each therefore contains its own negation. Everything that is, in any way, is only insofar as it contains contradiction within itself.

124.title: Ground
124.text: Ground is the unity of Identity and Difference — the reflection of Essence into itself as the positing of a presupposition. It is the foundation from which an Existence emerges, and apart from which that Existence is not what it is.

131.title: Appearance
131.text: Appearance is the Existence of Essence — the showing-forth of Essence in a world of things and relations, in which what appears is not merely immediate but is the manifestation of the Essential.

139.title: Essential Relation
139.text: Essential Relation is the relation of two terms which are not merely external to one another, but in which each is what it is only in its relation to the other. Its forms are Whole and Parts, Force and Manifestation, and Outer and Inner.

142.title: Actuality
142.text: Actuality is the unity of Essence and Existence — Being which has become identical with its own essence, so that what it is and that it is coincide. It is the ground of all determinate content, and the truth of the modal categories of possibility, contingency, and necessity.

160.title: The Concept
160.text: The Concept (Begriff) is the unity of Being and Essence — the self-determining universal which is not merely a form imposed on content from outside, but is itself the very content that it determines. It is free, self-moving, and identical with itself in the other.

163.title: The Concept as such
163.text: The Concept as such contains three moments: the Universal (the self-identical, the free), the Particular (determinacy), and the Individual (the singular, the concrete). These are not three separate concepts but one concept in three inseparable moments.

166.title: Judgment
166.text: Judgment is the division of the Concept — the self-diremption of the individual into subject and predicate, in which the universal is shown to be the ground of the individual, and the individual is shown to be the concrete realization of the universal.

181.title: The Syllogism
181.text: The Syllogism is the Concept as it has returned to itself through its own diremption — the unity of the two extremes (Universal and Individual) in the middle term (the Particular). The necessity of the conclusion is the necessity of the Concept itself.

194.title: Objectivity
194.text: Objectivity is the Concept as it has entered into immediate existence — the Concept in the form of an external manifold. Its forms are Mechanism, Chemism, and Teleology, in which the Concept progressively reasserts its own unity against the externality of its material.

213.title: The Idea
213.text: The Idea is the unity of the Concept and Objectivity — the Concept which has become identical with its own reality. It is the truth of everything actual: the correspondence of the Concept with its existence.

216.title: Life
216.text: Life is the Idea in its immediate form — the Concept realized in an organic body, in which the parts are what they are only in their relation to the whole, and the whole is the process of maintaining itself through its parts.

233.title: The Absolute Idea
233.text: The Absolute Idea is the unity of Life and Cognition — the Idea which has become conscious of itself as the whole of reality, and which thereby returns to itself as absolute self-knowledge. It is the truth of the entire Logic.

377.title: Spirit
377.text: Spirit is the Idea which has returned to itself out of its otherness — the self-knowing, self-determining Subject for whom the whole of reality is its own content. It is the truth of Nature and of Logic alike.

483.title: Objective Spirit
483.text: Objective Spirit is Spirit as it has posited itself in an external world — in right, morality, and ethical life, in the institutions of the family, civil society, and the state. Its truth is the rational freedom of the will in the objective order of the world.

553.title: Absolute Spirit
553.text: Absolute Spirit is Spirit knowing itself as absolute — the self-consciousness of the Idea in its threefold form of Art, Religion, and Philosophy. In it, Spirit is no longer divided from its own content, but is at one with it.

572.title: Philosophy
572.text: Philosophy is the highest form of Absolute Spirit — the self-thinking of the Idea, in which Spirit knows itself as the whole of reality, and the entire system returns to its own beginning in the pure self-knowledge of the Concept.
